text: Weston is a village in Wood County, Ohio, United States, with a population of 1,455 as recorded in the 2020 census. It is situated just 10 miles west of Bowling Green, Ohio, a university town. The village was originally named Taylortown and was platted in 1853 by Thomas Taylor, who it was named after. Another early name used was New Westfield. The current name derives from Weston Township. A post office named New Westfield was established in 1856 and was renamed Weston in 1863. The village was incorporated in 1873. According to the United States Census Bureau, Weston has a total area of 1.13 square miles (2.93 km²), all of which is land. As of the 2010 census, there were 1,590 people, 609 households, and 424 families residing in the village. The population density was 1,407.1 inhabitants per square mile (543.3/km²), with 700 housing units at an average density of 619.5 per square mile (239.2/km²). The racial composition was 91.6% White, 0.1% African American, 1.0% Native American, 0.1% Asian, 4.8% from other races, and 2.4% from two or more races. Hispanic or Latino of any race made up 11.8% of the population. Among households, 37.1% had children under 18, 49.4% were married couples living together, 15.6% had a female householder with no husband present, 4.6% had a male householder with no wife present, and 30.4% were non-families. Twenty-five point one percent of households consisted of individuals, and 8.3% had someone living alone who was 65 years or older. The average household size was 2.60, and the average family size was 3.07. The median age was 35.8 years, with 29.2% of residents under 18, 6.7% between 18 and 24, 26.8% aged 25 to 44, 26.4% aged 45 to 64, and 10.9% 65 years or older. The gender distribution was 49.4% male and 50.6% female. In the 2000 census, there were 1,659 people, 638 households, and 454 families. The population density was 1,476.2 inhabitants per square mile (570.0/km²), with 662 housing units at an average density of 589.1 per square mile (227.5/km²). The racial makeup was 93.31% White, 0.18% African American, 0.12% Native American, 0.12% Asian, 3.74% from other races, and 2.53% from two or more races. Hispanic or Latino of any race accounted for 9.10% of the population. The Weston Public Library serves communities in southwestern Wood County from administrative offices in Weston and a branch in Grand Rapids. In 2006, the library loaned 96,919 items, provided 186 programs to its 3,399 cardholders, and had total holdings of over 35,000 volumes with over 130 periodical subscriptions.
